title: Length under last-coordinate restriction
statement: Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$, and let $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ be real-valued functions on that cube. For every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and bit $b$, the square root of $P(f(x,b))^2$, plus the sum of the squares of all coordinate derivatives of $f$ at $(x,b)$ and the squares of all $g_j(x,b)$, equals the square root of $P(f_b(x))^2+(D_{n+1}f(x,b))^2$ plus the squared length of the vector consisting of the first $n$ derivatives of $f_b$ and the values of the restrictions $(g_j)_b$ at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a real-valued function on the (n+1)-dimensional Boolean cube
g is an m-tuple of real-valued functions on that cube
x is a point of the n-dimensional Boolean cube
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, a real function $h$ on a uniform Boolean cube, and a vector $k$ of real functions on that cube, put $V(h,k)(x)=((D_i h(x))_i,(k_j(x))_j)$ and $F_P(h,k)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(h)^2+\|V(h,k)\|_2^2}$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference. Let $f$ be a real function and $g$ a vector of $m$ real functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $g_b(x)=g(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and define $a_g,d_g$ componentwise. For every $x,b$, $\sqrt{P(f(x,b))^2+\|V(f,g)(x,b)\|_2^2}=\sqrt{P(f_b(x))^2+d_f(x)^2+\|V(f_b,g_b)(x)\|_2^2}$.
